content.value_statement: Dart primary constructors introduce new syntax and scoping rules that can make migrations difficult. This skill explains the rules and guides correct refactoring from traditional constructors.
actual_capabilities: Explains Dart version requirements for primary constructors.
Shows declaring, initializing, and regular parameter forms.
Explains primary initializer scope and late-field restrictions.
Migrates eligible traditional constructors to primary constructor syntax.
Converts eligible in-body constructors to redirecting constructors.
Explains abbreviated new, const new, and factory constructor syntax.
limitations: It documents syntax and does not run the Dart analyzer or compiler.
It cannot determine whether primary constructors are enabled in a project.
It does not change files unless the AI tool is separately asked to edit them.
It covers the described Dart primary-constructor feature, not all Dart migration work.

use_cases.title: Learn the new syntax
use_cases.description: Understand primary constructor declarations, fields, and empty-body shorthand before using the feature.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Flutter model
use_cases.description: Convert a simple data model from a traditional generative constructor to a primary constructor.

use_cases.title: Resolve migration diagnostics
use_cases.description: Interpret common initialization and late-field errors while adopting the new constructor forms.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a primary constructor
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain Dart primary constructors with a short example. State the minimum Dart version required.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a simple class
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this Dart class to a primary constructor when valid. Explain each change and preserve behavior: [paste class].

prompt_templates.title: Review constructor scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this primary constructor for initializer-scope and late-field errors. Identify invalid references and provide a corrected version: [paste class].

prompt_templates.title: Plan a safe migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan for these Dart classes. Identify classes eligible for primary constructors, redirecting constructor changes, and compiler checks: [paste files].

output_examples.input: Convert a User class with final name and age fields and a matching generative constructor.
output_examples.output: A compact primary constructor declaration that preserves the two final fields, followed by an explanation of declaring parameters.

output_examples.input: Why does a late field initializer not see my primary constructor parameter?
output_examples.output: An explanation that primary initializer scope applies to non-late field initializers, with options for restructuring the initialization.

output_examples.input: Review a class with a named secondary constructor after migration.
output_examples.output: A review that identifies whether the in-body constructor redirects to the primary constructor and describes the required correction.

best_practices: Confirm the project Dart version and experiment settings before migrating.
Run the Dart analyzer and tests after each constructor migration.
Keep non-late derived field initializers close to the primary constructor declaration.
anti_patterns: Do not use primary constructors in Dart versions that do not support them.
Do not reference primary constructor parameters from late field initializers.
Do not keep non-redirecting generative constructors beside a primary constructor.

faq.question: What Dart version supports primary constructors?
faq.answer: Dart 3.13 and later enable them by default. Dart 3.12 requires an experiment flag.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my source files?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and proposed refactorings. Your AI tool edits files only when separately instructed.

faq.question: Can a primary constructor declare fields?
faq.answer: Yes. Declaring parameters with final or var create corresponding instance fields.

faq.question: Can late field initializers use constructor parameters?
faq.answer: No. Primary initializer scope does not apply to late instance variable initializers.

faq.question: Can I keep another generative constructor?
faq.answer: In-body generative constructors must redirect to the primary constructor when the language rules require it.

faq.question: Does the skill validate compiled output?
faq.answer: No. Use the Dart analyzer, compiler, and project tests to validate a migration.
